item.title: ComfyUI-UML: diagrams as nodes, images and shareable source
item.description:
antoinebou12/ComfyUI-UML

★ 3 · 3 forks · Repository created 2026-02-23

GitHub statistics recorded October 20, 2026.

ComfyUI is useful beyond image generation when an intermediate result can become a node output. ComfyUI-UML applies that idea to diagrams: text enters a rendering node; an image, a saved file, and a shareable URL can leave it.

item.title: Inside BatchBacktesting: parallel runs, explicit assumptions and useful outputs
item.description:
AlgoETS/BatchBacktesting

★ 3 · 4 forks · Repository created 2023-03-29

GitHub statistics recorded October 20, 2026.

A batch backtest is a small data pipeline: choose instruments, obtain prices, clean the observations, run a strategy, and save comparable results. AlgoETS/BatchBacktesting makes those steps visible in Python rather than hiding them behind a dashboard.

This image is an existing article illustration, not a new benchmark run.

item.title: Teaching Python through an end-to-end data workshop
item.description:
AlgoETS/Workshop1

The most useful beginner workshop gives each new concept somewhere to go. AlgoETS/Workshop1 moves from Python setup to an API response, a DataFrame, and a chart. The final notebook uses Apple price data and exponential moving averages to bring those steps together.

item.title: Exploring movie similarities with vector search algorithms
item.description: I taught a thread on “find movies like this” that kept growing: embeddings in PostgreSQL, the same idea in Qdrant with two different vector meanings, then retrieval + a local LLM grounded on the same rows. This page is the story; notebooks and animations live in AlgoETS/SimilityVectorEmbedding. Version française.

item.title: Python library for MarketWatch virtual trading
item.description: I wanted to automate chores in MarketWatch’s virtual stock game (paper trading, not a real broker). marketwatch on PyPI is the small client I shipped — watchlists, game state, portfolio, orders, leaderboard. Version française.

item.title: A Method to Install Python Packages for Add-ons & Plugins in Blender (Windows, Blender 4.2+)
item.description: Blender add-ons that need NumPy, meshio, or requests hit the same wall: Blender ships its own Python, so system pip does nothing useful. I wrote a small installer that targets Blender’s sys.executable, drops wheels under scripts/modules, and runs in a background thread so the UI stays responsive (Blender 4.2+, Windows). Version française.

item.title: Multiple Technical Indicators Backtesting on Multiple Tickers using Python
item.description: Same BatchBacktesting engine as the earlier indicator experiment, but emphasized at portfolio scale: many tickers, two strategies, equities plus crypto, aggregate winners and losers. Version française.

item.title: Experimenting with technical indicators using Python and backtesting
item.description: I batch-ran EMA and MACD strategies across many tickers with BatchBacktesting — FMP for equities, Binance for crypto. This post explains what the runner does, how to read outrageous leaderboard rows, and why that is not a live trading system. Version française.

item.title: Predicting Stock Prices with Monte Carlo Simulations
item.description: Trading is about ranges, not one magic price. I used forward Monte Carlo on Apple daily closes: estimate log-return drift and volatility before 2023, simulate many paths, then check whether 2023 hold-out prices fell inside a 5th–95th percentile band. Version française.
